newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi says mulls support to affiliates.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi says mulls support to affiliates.

text.p: Japan's fourth biggest broker Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd said on Friday that it is considering providing support to financially troubled non-bank affiliates.
But details have yet to be decided, it said.

Ryuji Shirai, deputy president at Yamaichi, said the bank has been reviewing the 10-year programme it launched three years ago to help restructure its non-bank affiliates and may shorten that period. Last month, Nomura Securities Co Ltd said it would post a special loss of 371 billion yen in the half year because it would provide aid to a troubled non-bank.

Earlier today, Yamaichi revised its parent current profit forecast down to 6.5 billion yen for the first six months of 1996/97 ended on September 30 from the previous forecast of 15 billion yen. In the first half of 1995/96, Yamaichi posted a 5.21 billion yen parent current profit.
Shirai said the revision reflected the sluggish stock market in the summer, which reduced income from stockbroking fees and profits from stock trading.
However, he said Tokyo's stock market would see more active trade in the latter half of 1996/97, supported by the continuation of the central bank's easy monetary stance.
